This idea is inspired by this post.

There have been many attempts to fix Voat's current downvotes system, on account of the fact that they have the power to limit certain users to a specific number of posts per day. This limitation was only ever intended to affect spammers. From the announcement I just linked to:

They are old rules, mostly remaining unchanged from the initial versions of this site. Most, if not all, of the rules were in direct response to spam attacks. It was never Voat’s intention to limit non-spam accounts, but this is what has happened as an indirect result of these rules.

However, after a thousand comments in that thread, nothing was done -- as no solution could be found that stopped the potential for limiting non-spam accounts without either giving real spammers free reign, or centralizing the control method. (Sidenote: Most of the non-spammers who complain about these restrictions go out of their way to stir shit all so that they can turn around and complain about Voat, so I don't have much sympathy left for those types).

However, downvotes have another "power" -- they can control what content can be seen. If enough downvotes are piled onto a comment or submission (this is more important concerning submissions) that submission's overall score will be lowered, and the usual handful of upvotes it will get from the dedicated campers in /v/all/new will be insufficient to boost the submission into /v/all for others to see. This will happen regardless of whether or not the submission is something the majority of users would have been interested in seeing or discussing. Sometimes these initial downvotes are a result of the /v/all/new campers personally disagreeing with the post, thus dooming it to never being seen by those who might agree; or they are a result of dedicated content controllers. In either case, just a handful of downvotes have the power to completely alter what Voat's front page will ultimately look like every hour. I fail to see how this is in the interest of open and honest discussion.

So here is my idea, a bit of a modification of the idea suggested in the first link supplied above. Note, this may be a major change and I have not reflected on it for long hours, so I may have overlooked something, but in essence I think the idea has promise.

First, remove essentially all power from downvotes (there's more, just bear with me). So (negative) CCP would no longer be the deciding factor concerning how often users can post. Positive CCP restrictions would still be in place for all the old reasons (need to contribute before you can downvote {although this first one wouldn't have to be the case if this idea is implemented; CCP would just be required for use of spam votes, see below}, or post submissions, or send messages, etc).

Second, introduce a new button (or modify an existing one) that can be applied to every comment and submission. A "spam" or "report spam" button. Every user would have a very limited number of these per day. Maybe the total number users have can increase with CCP, or maybe it can be the same for everyone. I don't know which would be best. I don't think this number should ever be over 100 though, and something like 5 or 10 would probably be best. By rationing the use of this "spam" vote or button, users will be forced to reserve their daily "spam" votes for actual spam (if they have any interest in curtailing spam, as fortunately most users so). There will inevitably be some users who try to use these "spam" votes against non-spamming users. This is why the feature should be designed so that something like 20 different users have to have applied a spam vote to a spammer before what we currently call negative CCP restrictions would come into play. So if 20 different Voat users (or 50, or whatever) apply their spam vote to a spammer, that spammer will then be limited to 10 posts a day.

Maybe these restrictions will only be active for one week, and then a user's Spam Points (SP) will reset to zero. So if a user accumulates 20 or more SP over the course of a week, they are limited. The week gives Cyna or Putt time to evaluate the relevant spam reports and ban the user if they are an actual spammer, during which time they will struggle to continue spamming. Maybe /u/kevdude's old suggestion that the 10 posts a day be lowered to 3 per day (which I always opposed for our current system, since non-spammers get hit by these restrictions) would make sense with this idea, since at most the user is limited for one week, unless they spam again. It would also further limit the spammer's ability to spam during that week while someone is evaluating the spam report.

I'm not done. Since all users are significantly limited in their use of spam votes, and everyone will clearly understand the purpose of the spam votes (unlike is the case with downvotes, where all users use them somewhat differently), then penalties can be applied to those who use them for purposes other than curtailing spam. So if a user uses all 10 of their daily spam votes on an innocent user who obviously was in no way spamming (even though this would only increase the innocent user's SP by 1, since SP requires 20 different persons to vote to accumulate 20 SP), some penalty will apply to the user who tried to suppress an innocent user (this step would unfortunately require manual intervention from someone like Cyna or Putt, but it's really no different from the process already used to manually ban spammers). Maybe the first time this penalty will be posting restrictions, similar to those applied by accumulating 20 SP. Maybe the second time, the user gets banned. Spam is a Voat bannable offence, so why shouldn't false accusations of spam be bannable (especially if you have two or three strikes)? Just like women who falsely accuse men of rape; they should be punished in the same way an actual rapist would be, no?

So what does this system really accomplish?

  • It still gives users the power to suppress spam. It does not centralize this power.
  • It forces users to be more responsible with their spam suppression activities (they have very limited spam votes every day, and they risk being restricted or banned if they try to spam-suppress non-spammers)
  • It (should) prevent non-spammers from ever being suppressed in terms of their daily ability to contribute on this free speech platform
  • It stops giving users the power to suppress content they don't like. Only upvotes will determine how high a post gets ranked (downvotes will still be displayed, so everyone can see how many people disagree, but only those who agree have the power to get it to the front page. Disagreement can be then expressed further in comment form within the thread).

So if someone posts a discussion that gets 2 upvotes and 2 downvotes, it probably won't make it to /v/all. If someone posts something that gets 100 upvotes and 90 downvotes, it probably will make it to /v/all. The only problem I see with this is the following: fake news or malicious links. At present downvotes can't only suppress spam and unpopular content; they can also suppress fake news or malicious links. However, I think that only the suppression of spam and malicious links is critical, and the suppression of unpopular content is egregious. The suppression of fake news is borderline Orwellian...because what if we're wrong about it being fake? Most times we're right, sure -- but the downvotes will still be there. Everyone will be able to see the 90 downvotes (unlike reddit where they hide that information). Anyone with a brain will look at a score of +100/-90 and know that something is up and maybe they should take the post with a grain of salt (or suspect vote manipulation of some kind). In my experience, we seldom get posts with +100/-90 anyway; fake news (like the old awdnews stuff) usually gets manipulated into the 200s or 300s, and Voat users can usually get close to 100 downvotes on it, but at that point it's still on the front page anyway.

I think this system will fix all the problems we have with non-spamming user suppression and content control, without taking away our power to deal with spam. If I overlooked something please point it out.
